programme.sub-title: A Time Machine Ride Back to the Past - Gwanghwamun Gate
programme.desc: On August 15, 2010, Gwanghwamun, the main gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace, was re-inaugurated. This gate, heavily damaged and altered during Japanese rule, was at last restored to its original appearance, and is now re-opened in full glory.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: The Hanyang City Wall in Seoul, a Rest Area for Seoulites
programme.desc: After King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty, moved the capital of his country to Hanyang (present day Seoul), he constructed the Hanyang City Wall (18.6 ㎞). The wall connected the four surrounding mountains and served as protection for the capital city.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: The Inwangsan Section of the Hanyang City Wall in Seoul, the Natural Landscape…
programme.desc: The Inwangsan Section of the Hanyang City Wall in Seoul extends from Sungnyemun Gate to Changuimun Gate. It was closed in 1968 following a failed attack on the Blue House by armed guerrillas from North Korea, and was not reopened to the public until 1993. Inwangsan Mountain is renowned for the unusual shapes of its granite rocks, and the impressive view of downtown Seoul from the fortress wall.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: Namhansanseong, the Masterpiece Fortress of the Joseon Dynasty
programme.desc: Registered on the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, Namhansanseong Fortress was built to protect Hanyang, the capital city of the Joseon Dynasty.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.desc: Jongmyo, the shrine where the memorial tablets of past kings and queens are housed, was one of the most majestic and sacred buildings of the Joseon dynasty. Its architecture visually renders such Confucian values that are the guiding principles of Joseon's political philosophy as piety and propriety toward ancestors.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: Embracing the Magnificent View of Seoul, Samgaksan
programme.desc: Samgaksan Mountain is the summit of Bukhansan Mountain and is made up of three peaks. These biotite granite peaks, formed in the late Jurassic period, are beautiful granite domes of different shapes that make wonderful natural scenery.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: The old Seoul Station Building which keeps the history of modern Korea
programme.desc: Since the old Seoul Station Building is the Korea’s oldest railroad station building, shows the great beauty of architecture.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage
programme.sub-title: Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.desc: The East Wing of the Deoksugung Palace’s Seokjojeon Hall is the modern stone architecture which was built as the main hall of the imperial house after King Gojong proclaimed the Joseon Dynasty(1392-1910) the Daehan Empire in 1897. The building is decorated in places with the patterns of plum blossom, the symbol of the Daehan Empire.

programme.desc: After King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty, moved the capital of his country to Hanyang (present day Seoul), he constructed the Hanyang City Wall (18.6 ㎞). The wall connected the four surrounding mountains and served as protection for the capital city.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: The Inwangsan Section of the Hanyang City Wall in Seoul, the Natural Landscape…
programme.desc: The Inwangsan Section of the Hanyang City Wall in Seoul extends from Sungnyemun Gate to Changuimun Gate. It was closed in 1968 following a failed attack on the Blue House by armed guerrillas from North Korea, and was not reopened to the public until 1993. Inwangsan Mountain is renowned for the unusual shapes of its granite rocks, and the impressive view of downtown Seoul from the fortress wall.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: Namhansanseong, the Masterpiece Fortress of the Joseon Dynasty
programme.desc: Registered on the tentative list of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, Namhansanseong Fortress was built to protect Hanyang, the capital city of the Joseon Dynasty.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.desc: Jongmyo, the shrine where the memorial tablets of past kings and queens are housed, was one of the most majestic and sacred buildings of the Joseon dynasty. Its architecture visually renders such Confucian values that are the guiding principles of Joseon's political philosophy as piety and propriety toward ancestors.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: Embracing the Magnificent View of Seoul, Samgaksan
programme.desc: Samgaksan Mountain is the summit of Bukhansan Mountain and is made up of three peaks. These biotite granite peaks, formed in the late Jurassic period, are beautiful granite domes of different shapes that make wonderful natural scenery.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage : Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.sub-title: The old Seoul Station Building which keeps the history of modern Korea
programme.desc: Since the old Seoul Station Building is the Korea’s oldest railroad station building, shows the great beauty of architecture.

programme.title: A trip to Seoul's cultural heritage
programme.sub-title: Seokjojeon Hall, Daehan Empire History Museum
programme.desc: The East Wing of the Deoksugung Palace’s Seokjojeon Hall is the modern stone architecture which was built as the main hall of the imperial house after King Gojong proclaimed the Joseon Dynasty(1392-1910) the Daehan Empire in 1897. The building is decorated in places with the patterns of plum blossom, the symbol of the Daehan Empire.

Launch of Borrowers’ Platform’s process
programme.desc: During the week of the IMF–World Bank Spring Meetings in Washington, DC, the Ministers of Finance and Central Bank Governors of developing countries will launch the Borrowers’ Platform to improve their debt management capacity. The initiative is Member State-led, with UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) serving as the secretariat.

programme.title: Co-creating a Better Future: Advancing the Global Dialogue on Technology and Research (CPD59 Side Event)
programme.desc: This signature side-event at CPD59 will convene Member States, UN entities, youth leaders, and private sector partners to advance concrete action, collaboration and investment-readiness to technological innovation and research breakthroughs that accelerate the implementation of the ICPD PoA.

programme.title: Demographic Shifts, Digital Futures, and Sustainable Development: Realizing the Silver Dividend (CPD59 Side Event)
programme.desc: As populations age worldwide, demographic change is reshaping economies, labour markets, and social systems. This side event will examine how the “silver dividend” can be harnessed through digital innovation, inclusive technologies, and research-driven policymaking to advance sustainable development.

programme.title: Inclusive Data for Culturally Diverse Gender Identities: Lessons from Mexico’s Muxes (CPD59 Side Event)
programme.desc: This side event will share the lived experience of a Muxe woman and explore how inclusive data practices, research and technology can support evidence-based policy-making in line with the ICPD Programme of Action and the Sustainable Development Goals.

programme.title: From Users to Co-Architects: Advancing ICPD Commitments for and with Youth in a Digital Age (CPD59 Side Event)
programme.desc: This side event of the fifty-ninth session of the Commission on Population and Development (CPD59) seeks to sustain the momentum of the Cotonou Youth Action Agenda and the 2024 ICPD30 Global Dialogue on Technology, emphasizing that a digital future must be equitable and co-engineered with the people who navigate it daily.

programme.title: Chasing Bliss
programme.desc: Water is life, and the great conductor that connects us all. The oceans cover over 70% of our planet and hold almost 97% of the earth's water. True bliss in constant movement giving life around the globe. This is a story of an eclectic mix of people across Hawaii, Ecuador and the USA, who draw energy from this life force and channel it positively into their everyday lives. Join Paulino in understanding what drives Surfer Laid Hamilton, or filmmaker Robert Greaves, Big-Wave World Champion Paige Alms and Windsurfing World Record Holder Sarah Hauser. Coffee Farmer Anti Clancy, Dr Greg Mitchell, Research Scientist & Algae Visionary at Scripps.

programme.title: Connections Between Science & Philosophy
programme.desc: Dr. Menas Kafatos is internationally known for bridging the disciplines, writing and lecturing extensively on the convergence between science and philosophy, as there is an inherent need for a dialogue between science, spirituality, and religion. His book, Creating Cosmos with Deepak Chopra discusses the melding of topics like inflation, environmental issues, natural hazards, quantum theory and consciousness.

programme.title: Iranian Space Pioneer
programme.desc: Iranian electrical engineer, entrepreneur and former astronaut, Anousheh Ansari was the first female private space explorer to fly to the International Space Station. She explains the challenging journey and the determination needed to reach space after immigrating to the U.S. from Iran. She also became the first person to publish a blog from space. The content invited readers to share her experience with the world. She described the Russian Soyuz capsule during liftoff, talked about the sights and smells of the space station, and explained the intricacies of everyday activities.

programme.title: Philosopher of the Mind
programme.desc: Dr. Paavo Pylkknens eclectic approach combines new physics-based insights with those of analytical philosophy, phenomenology, cognitive science and neuroscience. He proposes a view in which the mechanistic framework of classical physics and neuroscience is complemented by a more holistic approach. Pylkknen is particularly known for his work on mind-body-studies, building on David Bohm's interpretation of quantum mechanics.

programme.title: Evolution of Ideas
programme.desc: Everything we can know about our lives and the universe is a subjective experience, either formed by one's own perceptions or the reports of others. Dr. Bernardo Kastrup explains how we commonly associate this understanding about the universe as something separate of our consciousness, however he strongly believes otherwise; Kastrup believes the evolution of ideas we perceive about the universe are actually originating within us.

programme.title: Book Of Knowledge
programme.desc: Traveling the world 30+ years, David Verdesi finds himself back in Rome. Urged to uncover the reason behind the instinctive human desire for spiritual yearning, Verdesi starts retracing the intersection of science and theology within the city his family has called home since the early 1400s. Vibrating from the walls of the citys sacred spaces, he discovers findings of oral history, predating the beginning of humanity by thousands of years. Documents and rare rituals that upend conventional ideas of the behaviors of the mind in ancient times. Narratives heavily influenced by civilizations and cultures beyond Rome, continue to influence the moral compass of life today, Verdesi realizes he is back on the road. Book of Knowledge The Quest for Meaning rediscovers and preserves the knowledge of our human potential and natures wisdom. This movie addresses questions around the intersection of science, spirituality, and anthropology. Join David Verdesi to the roots of the Book of Knowledge.

programme.title: Across the Ice
programme.desc: After 45+ expeditions throughout over 150+ countries, one of the world's leading adventurers and visionaries of conservation, Swedish explorer Johan Ernst Nilson dawns upon his biggest adventure yet. Follow his journey across the planet from the North Pole to the South Pole in Pole2Pole. The 525 day mostly carbon-neutral trek covers 20,000 miles by means of skis, dogsled, boat, bike and kite. Pole2Pole is not only one of the most difficult adventures hes ever attempted, but also one of his most philanthropic adventures. Johan visits charities along the way to share their stories and raise global awareness.

programme.title: Particle Physics
programme.desc: At only 21, Frank Wilczek, a graduate student at Princeton University, defined the properties of color gluons, which hold atomic nuclei together while working with David Gross. He is known, among other things, for the discovery of asymptotic freedom, the development of quantum chromodynamics, the invention of axions, and the discovery and exploitation of new forms of quantum statistics (anyons).

programme.title: The Nature of All Things
programme.desc: What is it that makes things what they are? Where does it come from? For Professor Seyyed Hossein Nasr, the quest for knowledge, specifically knowledge which enables man to understand the true nature of things and which furthermore, liberates and delivers him from the fetters and limitations of earthly existence, has been (and continues to be) the central concern and determinant of how we understand and live our lives.

programme.title: Astrology Zone
programme.desc: Susan Miller is the founder and astrologist for AstrologyZone.com. The trusted, twenty-year-old platform provides the latest in intelligent astrological trends. This discussion with Deepak Chopra breaks down many popular misconceptions about astrological predictions, the various disciplines of study, ego, and consciousness in relation to astrology. Miller also outlines the golden rule to understanding and getting the most out of astrological predications: astrology shows the condition, but not the outcomethat outcome is completely up to you. I can give you questions to ask to help you decide, but in the end, you write the script of your life.

programme.title: Modern Metaphysical Idealism
programme.desc: Dr. Bernardo Kastrup, philosopher and author has been leading the modern renaissance of metaphysical idealism. His theoretical reflections on the mind explain consciousness as the only element of life that allows us to understand reality, and everything we know about reality is subject to our experiences. This idea is often refuted by the thought that the brain is the source, not images and experiences provided by consciousness.

programme.title: Nature, Space and Matter
programme.desc: Our understanding of the nature of time, space and matter have changedeven what we mean by these termsin just the last few decades. Our interpretations continue to change and more theories form as we learn and study these topics. Dr. Fred Alan Wolf explains the origins of many of these foundational theories that have formed at different times and why they came about. Before quantum physics, people knew that human beings were conscious. We knew that animals were conscious. But now, with new revelations in quantum physics we begin to see a new role for consciousness.

programme.title: Creation Is Constant
programme.desc: Duane Elgin wants to show that the universe is a living field of existence, and that we are always in communion with a field of aliveness whether we are conscious of it or not. Throughout this lecture, Elgin explains his belief that in a living system, each part is integral to the whole, so each entity is intimately connected to the entire universe. To him, creation is not something that happened with the Big Bang. Instead, creation is consistently forming around us from a deeper abyss. The universes existence is brought moment by moment through this continuous, moving process.

programme.title: Consciousness & Healing

programme.title: Pork, It’s What’s for Supper
programme.desc: Blaine is still in Florida and is looking to add pork to the menu. We also go behind the scenes on a different show and show you the hunt, then how it REALLY went down.

programme.title: The Bigfoot Mirror
programme.desc: Ryan Willis and Joel Porter visit Algonquin Highlands to perform a new tactic on their night investigation to summon a Bigfoot.

programme.title: The Perfect Hunt
programme.desc: On this hunt Daryl guides 5 clients and Claudio to 48 ducks and 48 geese to wrap up the perfect trip!

programme.title: Alaskan Salmon Run
programme.desc: Larysa Switlyk ventures off to Alaska to fill her freezer with salmon and shares her passion of fishing with Mark who was there to help film but later couldn’t take the fly rod out of his hand!

programme.title: Spruce Tree Root as Rope
programme.desc: Some Native Americans used the root of spruce trees as rope. Tune in to see Ryan Marshall demonstrate the technique.

programme.title: Forest Fires
programme.desc: Hosts Steve Hamilton and Kaylee Klassen chat with John Davies and Byron Wolf about the ongoing fires across the country.

programme.title: Missouri Cats, Coyotes and Coon
programme.desc: Join Matt Burson and his son Ethan as they pursue their passion of land trapping a mixed bag of critters in the state of Missouri. These two men are skilled, and theyll share their techniques with you today as the fur starts to pile up.

programme.title: Whitetail Rut in Texas: Feast or Famine - Part 1
programme.desc: Wade and Steve are going after whitetail during the peak of the rut. This episode is as unpredictable as a buck during the rut and we can't wait to bring you all the action

programme.title: Season 3, Episode 7
programme.desc: We’ve got a C21 update with Tracey Wilson, as well as some of the craziest clips we’ve had on the show ever!

programme.title: Agri-Trade Special
programme.desc: Agriculture technology and innovations at the Agri-Trade Equipment Expo in Red Deer, AB

programme.title: Illinois Whitetail
programme.desc: Every pastor needs to get away sometimes. The Rev gets away to Illinois for some rest and relaxation, and to hunt for whitetail.

programme.title: Whitetail Bow Hunting Across America
programme.desc: In this episode, we join Kevin on his first velvet whitetail hunt in Kentucky. We then join Wade in Central Texas as he meets up with an old friend to hunt whitetails in the Texas brush country.

programme.title: Moose on the Menu
programme.desc: Greg's hunting season doesn't go according to plan, but hunting seldom does. On this week's episode Greg and his good friends Kiley & Hailey Topliss try to fill their freezers with big game.

programme.title: Pennsylvania Red Fox Trapping - Day 2
programme.desc: Ken Patula and his trapping partner Bob, have found success on their Pennsylvania trapline. Among the beauty of the mountains and fall colors, they encounter some interesting characters that appear through the foggy, mountain mornings.

programme.title: Pure Passion Part 1 : Saskatchewan Black Bears
programme.desc: Join Brody and Amy Teale as they hunt and fish along the North Saskatchewan River with Pure Passion Outfitting.

programme.title: Trophy Pintails in Oregon
programme.desc: Mario and the local Oregon guys get together for a late season hunt in the Pacific NW. They pull out the layout boats for some high-water tricks to shoot some trophy Pintails and other ducks.

programme.title: Axis Hunting and a Waterbuck Adventure in South Africa
programme.desc: This week on Americana Outdoors, we're going to join Jeff Reynolds as he goes on a dream hunt for an axis buck and then we'll journey back to South Africa with Wade Middleton as he goes back into the field in search of a waterbuck.

programme.title: Winter Woes
programme.desc: Ben and Nicole have committed to a goal of self-sufficiency. Unfortunately, its proving harder than they thought. Homesteading isnt as glamourous as it may look online. Atlantic Canadian winters are proving more difficult than ever before

programme.title: Mom's Bear
programme.desc: Corey and his parents go bear hunting in the North Woods. It's moms first time chasing black bear.

programme.title: Island Pheasant
programme.desc: Your host Steve Elmy is going to take you on an awesome trip to the most southern inhabited island in Canada for an epic pheasant hunt

programme.title: Wild West Ducks & Nebraska Snows
programme.desc: The FA crew heads out on the famed Columbia River in Oregon to chase some birds, miles of places for the birds to hide and some incredible scenery. Then we slide into a little trip we took to Nebraska to hunt with the guys at Whiskey Sloughs.

programme.title: South Dakota
programme.desc: This week Clede Spooner and Matt Cowell head west in pursuit of two species they've never hunted

programme.title: Crazy Rut Hunting
programme.desc: November, the rut is on, and the Grigsby is home to some of the best whitetail hunting in the Midwest. Strap into your tree stand because you have to put the hours in to shoot a Booner

programme.title: The Midwest
programme.desc: his week Heath & Brandon head to the Midwest in pursuit of giant whitetails

programme.title: Spring Cleaning
programme.desc: As winter thaws Ben & Nicole set out to tidy up the yard and prep the garden. With cleanup well underway they pick up a new honeybee hive in hopes of being able to pollinate their garden and reap some sweet, sweet homegrown honey

programme.title: Hog Hunts and a Big Ten Point
programme.desc: This week on Americana Outdoors, we look at all the ways that you can hunt hogs and then we'll go on a whitetail adventure with Brian Flaherty of TenPoint Crossbows where he's going to encounter his best buck ever.

programme.title: Chasin' Whitetails: Manitoba Whitetail Deer
programme.desc: Join Troy Esau on an exciting journey as he tracks elusive mature whitetail deer throughout the Manitoba hunting season.

programme.title: Filling the Freezer
programme.desc: After a long 8 weeks the meat birds are finally ready for the freezer. Family and friends band together and join Ben & Nicole as they slaughter whats left of their chickens in hopes of being able to feed both them and Bens parents for the winter

programme.title: Arkansas Duck Hunting
programme.desc: The crew heads to the duck capital of the world with good friend Russell Roberson from Alpha Innovations

programme.title: South Dakota Pheasant & Jumping Asian Carp
programme.desc: The Green Way Outdoors team head to the pheasant capital of America, South Dakota. They hunt for pheasants and then head to the Missouri River to partake in some aerial Asian carp bowfishing!

programme.title: Fly Fishing the Grand Cascapedia
programme.desc: This week, Pierre and his buddy Pat are in Gaspesie, Quebec for some fly fishing at the legendary Grand Cascapedia River.

programme.title: Pacific Saltwater Bottom Fishing
programme.desc: Jigging spoons for BC coastal halibut and pacific cod

programme.title: Sunny Skies Where the Dove Dies
programme.desc: Loaded with Kent shells we hunt a few different locations and share some tips on what to look for when you want to get out and sharpen your skills before the waterfowl season

programme.title: Crazy Rut Hunting
programme.desc: November, the rut is on, and the Grigsby is home to some of the best whitetail hunting in the Midwest. Strap into your tree stand because you have to put the hours in to shoot a Booner

programme.title: The Clam" Before the Storm"
programme.desc: Capt. Ed Zyak is joined by long time TV host and Banana River native Capt. Blair Wiggins to visit Blair's home waters to find the famed flats unrecognizable. Human impact and runoff have taken their toll, but Capt. Blair and others have a plan.

programme.title: Turkey Hunting
programme.desc: Pierre goes to the administrative region of Estrie to meet his fellow guide Samuel L'Heureux who will show him the basics of turkey hunting.

programme.title: Wildfire Devastation
programme.desc: Rich and Sandi talk about the wild fire on the line and show the devastation caused.
